vocabulary.definition: specialized language used by specific groups, often difficult for others to understand
vocabulary.example: The scientists were discussing their research using a lot of jargon that I couldn't follow.
The teacher spent extra time glossing the complex mathematical concepts for the students.

vocabulary.definition: a verb followed by one or more particles (prepositions, adverbs) that together form a single semantic unit
vocabulary.example: Examples of phrasal verbs include 'give up', 'put off', and 'look forward to'.

vocabulary.definition: related to a city or town, especially in its administration; relating to citizenship or community affairs
vocabulary.example: The mayor announced a new civic initiative to improve public spaces in the city.

vocabulary.definition: the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region
vocabulary.example: The author captured the essence of the region by using the local vernacular in the dialogue of the characters.

vocabulary.definition: to accept or support something enthusiastically; to hug or hold closely
vocabulary.example: Despite initial reservations, she decided to embrace the new technology and found it quite useful.
